rules.problem: Every red-box criterion is covered and the trigger (Headache) is right. But the red box's 'Manage and refer urgently' names 'malaria likely' (fever now or in past 3 days, and in a malaria area in past 3 months), and the file has no malaria-area finding and no probable Malaria rule; the same 'malaria likely' appears again in the non-urgent flow. House rule: every 'X likely' becomes a probable diagnosis.

rules.rule: Check for causes of headache not needing urgent attention
rules.problem: Omits two page discriminators: 'headache worse on bending forward' (third sinusitis criterion) and 'been in a malaria area in past 3 months' (malaria likely). Everything listed is on the page and nothing is invented.
'consider stroke or TIA' -> possible is right; 'asymmetric' dropped (no concept), broader in the safe direction.

Page: recent common cold AND any of {thick nasal/postnasal discharge, pain on pushing forehead/cheeks, headache worse on bending forward}. The or-list is missing 'headache worse on bending forward', so a patient with cold + positional headache alone never gets Sinusitis likely. Structure and probable level otherwise faithful.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable tick bite fever in headache
rules.problem: Faithful: Yes-branch gate ((fever and body pain) or recent cold) plus tick bite -> likely. Does not require the sinusitis question to be No, which is lenient but matches the page's sequential flow well enough.

rules.rule: Diagnose possible acute viral infection in headache
rules.problem: 'If none of above' on the page also excludes 'in a malaria area in past 3 months' (malaria likely); the rule excludes only sinusitis signs and tick bite. Negation structure for the sinusitis question (no recent cold OR none of the signs) is faithful. possible is a defensible level for 'treat as'.

Page: recurrent, throbbing, disabling, with nausea or light/noise sensitivity, resolving completely within 72 hours, in a patient WITHOUT fever/body pain/recent cold. The rule keeps recurrent + throbbing + (nausea | photophobia | phonophobia) but drops 'disabling', the 72-hour resolution, and the No-branch gate, so it is broader than the page (fires alongside sinusitis/viral in a febrile patient). probable is right ('Migraine likely').

rules.rule: Diagnose probable tension headache in headache
rules.problem: Tightness around head OR generalised (pressure-like) pain -> Tension headache likely: faithful. Not gated on migraine = No, acceptable.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable muscular neck pain in headache
rules.problem: 'Constant aching pain, tender neck muscles' read as AND of both; a fair reading of a single descriptive cell. Myofascial neck pain is the closest concept.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable giant cell arteritis in headache
rules.problem: Page: 'Patient > 50 years, pain over temples' -> GCA likely. The rule has only Temporal headache; the age criterion is absent and the grammar cannot express patient age. As written, any adult with temple pain is labelled probable giant cell arteritis (CRP, same-day specialist discussion). Downgrade to possible or document the unexpressible criterion explicitly.

rules.rule: Urgent: headache with red-box danger signs
rules.problem: Urgent is justified by 'Give urgent attention'. (and Headache (or ...)) mirrors the box; pregnancy/postpartum<=1 week AND BP>=140/90 correctly nested; worsening AND more frequent correctly paired; meningitis via active_condition per house pattern. Weak spots are concept-level (Wakes up during night; persistent nausea missing) not structural.

summary: Most consequential: the giant cell arteritis rule drops 'Patient > 50 years' (the grammar cannot express age), so probable GCA fires on temporal headache at any adult age. Second: 'malaria likely' appears twice on the page (red-box management and the non-urgent flow) but there is no malaria finding or rule; the sinusitis rule is also missing 'headache worse on bending forward', and the migraine rule drops 'disabling', the 72-hour resolution and the no-fever gate. Nothing is invented: every condition traces to the page; concept-level weaknesses are 'Wakes up during night' for 'headache that wakes patient', persistent nausea not encoded beside persistent vomiting, and the ART/persistent qualifiers being approximations.
